Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 67 s. 2023 OCT HON. ARNOLD G. TENEDERO City Administrator City of Tabuk, Kalinga Dear Hon. Tenedero: This has reference to your letter dated 9 August 2023 requesting for this Departmen!s opinion on whether or not the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Kalinga may remove items from the Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) in the City Budget. Per your letter, the Local Finance Committee of the Provincial Government of Kalinga, after its technical review, recommended that Appropriation Ordinance No. 4, s. 2022 of Tabuk City shows substantial compliance with the provisions of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan, however, identified the allowable charging in the submitted budget and directed the substitution of projects under the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). It declared operative in part the Appropriation Ordinance No. 4, series of 2022. Hence, this request for opinion. At the outset, it is important to note that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan does not have the authority to directly remove items from the Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) in the Appropriation Ordinance passed by lower sanggunians. The review power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is merely to check whether or not the appropriation ordinance of the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan was passed within the bounds of the law. The only ground to declare the same invalid in whole or in part is when it is passed by the concerned Sanggunian in an ultra vires capacity as Section 56 (c) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is instructive: (c) If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

This was explained in DILG Opinion No. 56 s. 2021, citing DILG Legal Opinion No. 23 s. of 2013, to wit: In DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, series of 2013, we had the opportunity to state that: aside from the fact that the sangguniang panlalawigan is bound to limit its review of the appropriation ordinance to the requirements set forth by the aforementioned provisions of the Code, Section 56(c) thereof is clear in providing for the only ground upon which a city ordinance or resolution may be declared invalid by the sangguniang panlalawigan i.e., the ordinance is beyond the power conferred upon the sanggunian concerned. In relation thereto, the case of Moday vs. CA (G.R. No. 107916, 20 February 1997) is instructive. In the said case, the Supreme court, citing Velasco vs. Blas (G.R. No. L-30456, 20 July 1982) ruled that: 'The only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance or order is 'beyond the power conferred upon the council or president making the same'. Absolutely, no other is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council, or president. Such has been consistent course of executive authority." From the foregoing, it is understood that the budgetary process at the local level follows a hierarchical structure, with different levels of local government having their own responsibilities and limitations. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan's primary role is to oversee lower-level LGUs' budgetary process and ensure compliance with the law rather than directly intervening in the budgeting decisions of cities or other LGUs. That does not include an authority to intervene with the budgetary process of the lower level sanggunians or component LGUs. We hope to have addressed your concern sufficiently. Thank you. truly yours, By thority of the Secr tary: . JUAN VICTOR R.
